speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; to begin our assessment, how long have these symptoms been occurring?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Esophageal Rupture).

The history of forceful retching following excessive alcohol consumption, followed by sudden chest pain and the inability to communicate, is highly suggestive of a tear in the esophagus. I will now request a Chest_X-Ray to look for pneumomediastinum or pleural effusion to confirm this diagnosis.
